claims.text: Traditional synthesis of single-phase ZrB2 requires temperatures above 2300 °C.
Adding multiple refractory transition-metal diborides to ZrB2 can produce a high-entropy metal diboride.
The proposed high-entropy diboride can form as a homogeneous ceramic at approximately 1700 °C.
The multi-cation diboride phase is stabilized by configurational entropy.
Multiple metal cations are randomly distributed within the diboride lattice.
The random multi-cation distribution creates lattice distortion.
The multi-cation composition modifies grain boundaries.
Lattice distortion and grain-boundary modification refine the microstructure.
Lattice distortion and grain-boundary modification enhance phase stability.
Configurational entropy suppresses grain growth during lower-temperature processing.
The high-entropy diboride creates intrinsic barriers to oxygen penetration.
The high-entropy diboride creates intrinsic barriers to metal-ion diffusion.
Barriers to oxygen penetration improve oxidation durability.
Barriers to metal-ion diffusion improve resistance to liquid-metal corrosion.
The high-entropy diboride processed at approximately 1700 °C will have mechanical strength comparable or superior to conventionally processed single-phase ZrB2.
The high-entropy diboride processed at approximately 1700 °C will retain structural integrity comparable or superior to single-phase ZrB2.
The high-entropy diboride will exhibit markedly better oxidation resistance than conventional high-temperature ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature ZrB2 specimens.
The high-entropy diboride will exhibit better liquid-metal corrosion durability than conventional high-temperature ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature ZrB2 specimens.
The anticipated benefits apply near a 1700 °C processing temperature under a controlled inert or reducing atmosphere.
The anticipated service benefits apply under high-temperature oxidizing conditions and prolonged liquid plating-metal exposure.
